annotations.text:
THE POSTS ARE THE CONTENT — three ways to show them.

The previous set was a news reader: text-led lists with postage-stamp thumbnails. Wrong for a media app. All three of these lead with the media, and all three still group by interest, because a person-follow must never widen the feed (FR-033).

A · MOSAIC
One section per interest, posts in a varied mosaic — a large tile with two small ones, alternating side each section so it never reads as a plain grid. Four posts visible per interest, ~8 per screen.

Trade: mixed tile sizes mean crops you don't control.

B · SHELVES
One shelf per interest: scroll DOWN through your interests, sideways through the posts inside one. Roughly a dozen posts reachable without a tap, and a quiet interest is obvious because its shelf is short.

Trade: portrait tiles suit some media badly; sideways scrolling hides posts off-screen.

C · IMMERSIVE
The post fills the screen. Sideways moves between interests, down moves through the posts inside one — the axis you swipe IS the organising principle.

Trade: one post at a time, so browsing is slower and the interest structure is felt rather than seen.
